articles.headline: OFAC Designates Entities and Individuals for Counter Narcotics and Counter Terrorism Activities
body: The U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced new designations on November 13, 2026, targeting individuals and entities involved in counter narcotics and counter terrorism activities.
These actions aim to disrupt illicit financial networks that support dangerous criminal and terrorist organizations globally, reinforcing the U.S. commitment to combating these threats.
Further details regarding the specific individuals and entities designated, as well as the implications of these designations, are available on the Treasury's website.

articles.headline: OFAC Issues Update to Iran Designations
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) released an update to its Iran designations on November 9, 2026.
This update includes modifications to existing listings and may involve new entries or clarifications regarding entities and individuals previously sanctioned under Iran-related authorities.
The Treasury Department continues to adjust its sanctions programs to address evolving threats and ensure the effectiveness of its measures against the Iranian regime.

articles.headline: New Iran-related Designations Announced by OFAC
body: OFAC announced new Iran-related designations on November 6, 2026, as part of its ongoing efforts to pressure the Iranian government.
These designations target specific individuals and entities deemed to be supporting the Iranian regime's destabilizing activities.
The U.S. Treasury Department continues to utilize its sanctions tools to counter Iran's proliferation of weapons, support for terrorism, and human rights abuses.

articles.headline: OFAC Imposes Cyber-related, Transnational Criminal, and Cuba Designations; Publishes Cuba-related Determination
body: On November 5, 2026, OFAC announced a series of designations targeting cyber-related malicious actors, transnational criminal organizations, and entities and individuals connected to Cuba.
The Cuba designations include a determination extending Executive Order 14404 to four additional sectors of the Cuban economy: manufacturing, technology, electronics, and marine.
This action allows the U.S. government to block property of non-U.S. persons operating in these newly covered sectors, further escalating economic pressure on the Cuban regime.

articles.headline: OFAC Announces Iran-related Designations, Updates, Alert, and Amended Venezuela GL
body: OFAC issued new Iran-related designations on November 4, 2026, alongside updates to existing listings and the publication of an Iran-related OFAC Alert.
Additionally, an amended Venezuela-related General License and a corresponding Frequently Asked Question were released, indicating adjustments to U.S. policy concerning Venezuela.
These actions reflect the Treasury's dynamic approach to sanctions, adapting to geopolitical developments and ensuring the clarity of its guidance.

articles.headline: OFAC Issues Amended Iran-related General License
body: On October 29, 2026, OFAC announced the issuance of an amended Iran-related General License.

General Licenses are often issued to authorize certain transactions that would otherwise be prohibited by sanctions, typically for humanitarian purposes or to facilitate specific types of legitimate trade.
The amendment aims to clarify or expand the scope of permissible activities under the existing Iran sanctions program.

articles.region: North Korea, Democratic Republic of the Congo
articles.headline: OFAC Designates Entities and Individuals Related to North Korea and DRC
body: OFAC announced new designations on October 28, 2026, targeting entities and individuals connected to North Korea and the Democratic Republic of the Congo.
These actions underscore the U.S. commitment to countering illicit activities that undermine regional stability and human rights.
The designations aim to disrupt financial networks supporting North Korea's weapons programs and those involved in corruption and human rights abuses in the DRC.

articles.headline: OFAC Amends FAQs on Blocking, Rejecting Transactions, and Reporting
body: On October 26, 2026, OFAC issued amended Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs) regarding blocking and rejecting transactions and filing reports with OFAC.
These amendments provide updated guidance for financial institutions and other entities on their compliance obligations under U.S. sanctions programs.
The revisions aim to enhance clarity and ensure consistent application of OFAC's regulations.

articles.headline: EU Imposes New Sanctions on Russia Targeting Cyber Activities and Financial Sector
body: The Council of the European Union announced new restrictive measures on November 16, 2026, adding 30 individuals and two entities to its sanctions list in response to Russia's malicious cyber activities and foreign information manipulation.

Among the designated entities is the Social Design Agency (SDA), a Moscow-based public relations and political technology company accused of orchestrating large-scale information manipulation and interference projects funded by the Russian Presidential Administration.

The sanctions also target the pro-Russian hacker group NoName057(16), responsible for cyber-attacks on critical infrastructure and government bodies in Ukraine, the United States, and EU member states, including the energy, financial, and transport sectors.

articles.headline: EU Expands Sanctions on Russia's Banking Sector and 'Shadow Fleet'
body: The European Union imposed additional restrictive measures on November 16, 2026, targeting 12 individuals and 101 entities for their role in supporting Russia's war of aggression against Ukraine.
These listings include nearly 50 Russian banks and financial institutions, aiming to further cut off financial channels that fund Russia's war effort.
The new sanctions also address Russia's 'shadow fleet' operations and other economic sectors providing substantial revenue to the Russian government.

articles.headline: UK Imposes Shipping and Trade Sanctions on Vessels Linked to Russian Oil and LNG
body: The UK government announced new shipping and trade sanctions on November 12, 2026, targeting specific vessels suspected of involvement in activities destabilizing Ukraine or supporting the Russian government.
One designated vessel, IMO 9630028, is suspected of carrying liquefied natural gas (LNG) of Russian origin from Russia to a third country.

Another vessel, IMO 9274616 (APEKS), an oil tanker, is believed to be involved in transporting Russian oil or oil products from Russia to a third country, leading to prohibitions on various services related to these ships.

articles.headline: UK Inflation Rises to 3.6% in October, Driven by Fuel Prices
body: UK inflation, as measured by the Consumer Prices Index (CPI), rose to 3.6% in October, up from 3.5% in September, marking its highest level in a year.
The increase was primarily driven by rising petrol and diesel prices, which saw an annual rate increase of 33.2%, the largest since July 2022.
Economists anticipate further increases, with the Bank of England forecasting inflation to peak near 5% next year, potentially leading to another interest rate hike in December.
articles.source: The Guardian / ITV News / Morningstar UK

articles.headline: Euro Area Annual Inflation Reaches 4.0% in October
body: The annual inflation rate in the euro area increased to 4.0% in October 2026, up from 3.8% in September, according to Eurostat.
Energy prices were the largest contributor to the rise, adding 1.89 percentage points to the annual rate, followed by services at 1.55 percentage points.
Compared to September, annual inflation fell in nine Member States, remained stable in two, and rose in sixteen, with Romania, Lithuania, and Bulgaria recording the highest rates.

articles.headline: Trump Signs Trade Deal with Thailand, Eliminating Tariffs on US Exports
body: U.S. President Donald Trump signed a trade deal with Thailand on November 17, 2026, which he hailed as 'historic,' stating that Thailand will eliminate all tariffs on U.S. exports.
The agreement also includes the removal of substantial non-tariff barriers and is expected to lead to Thailand purchasing an additional $2.6 billion in U.S. agricultural products.
The deal aims to lay the foundation for a much stronger trading relationship between the two countries, with further details of a formal agreement expected in the coming weeks.

articles.headline: Streamlining Export Controls for Drone Exports
body: The Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) is easing export controls on certain Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs or drones) and related parts, components, accessories, attachments, technology, and software under the Export Administration Regulations (EAR). Specifically, this rule: eliminates wind gust tolerance as a parameter for determining UAV controls under the EAR; increases the threshold for national security controls on certain UAVs from an endurance of 30 minutes to an endurance of 3 hours; makes conforming changes to remove national security controls on software and technology associated with UAVs with an endurance less than 3 hours; maintains military end-use and end-user controls on those lower endurance drones and associated software and technology; clarifies Commerce Control List (CCL) controls for certain UAVs specially designed for military use; and removes national security controls on certain specially designed parts, components, accessories, and attachments for such UAVs as they do not provide any significant military or intelligence capabilities.
